mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces the present value of expected equity returns, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression controlling for inflation and GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) below 5% in the prior month coincides with a contraction in labor market strength, which suppresses corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when UNRATE < 5%, or the effect is not robust (p > 0.05) in a panel of labor and equity data.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a shift toward services-driven growth, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
regime_hint: transition from manufacturing to services dominance
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the baseline (p > 0.05) when the HOUST/INDPRO pattern persists.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 suggests expanding supply capacity, which typically precedes a flattening or inversion of the S&P 500 20-day forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO is above 105 for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure that reduces investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are also negative when CPIAUCSL shows a similar surprise in the prior month, indicating no spillover effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (PAYEMS) below 7 million coincides with a contraction in labor market breadth, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 7 million in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when PAYEMS remains below 7 million for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail and industrial demand (HOUST and INDPRO both rising) suggests a robust macroeconomic recovery, which is expected to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies show simultaneous strength.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for three consecutive months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO remains below 100 for only one month.
